15. What is meant by “antigen-presenting cell,” and which cells
in the body can serve this function?
When a pathogen or foreign material invades and is en-
gulfed by a cell, the MHC molecule selects fragments of 
it, transports them to the cell surface, and displays them 
for the T cells. Th e cell that picked up the invader has now 
become an antigen-presenting cell (APC). Th e term APC 
refers to a cell that presents the antigen alerting the B and
T cells to the presence of a “non-self” substance. Mono-
cytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells are types of 
antigen-presenting cells.
16. What is the immune function of the lymphatic system?
Th e major functions of the lymphatic system are to concen-
trate antigens from all over the body into a few lymphoid 
organs, to circulate lymphocytes through lymphoid organs 
in order to allow antigens to interact with antigen-speciﬁ c 
cells, and to carry antibodies and other immune cells to the 
bloodstream and tissues.
